findings.F1: The gain sits only in the largest scaled moves: among active bars, the top quintile of |day's return / 20-day volatility| (mean |z| 1.87) earns 0.00477 a bar before fees (t 2.77, n 574) and 0.00406 after fees. The four lower quintiles earn 0.00009 to 0.00103 before fees against fees of 0.00031 to 0.00053, so three of the four lose net (-0.00022, -0.00010, -0.00040).
findings.F2: Fees eat 42% of the gain: across all bars they cost 0.000279 a bar against a gross gain of 0.000669. Trades come at 0.40 per bar, and in ETH's deepest fall the fees summed to 0.23 against a gain sum of -0.12.
findings.F3: Among high-volatility bars in the top two |z| quintiles, the move back holds only when the day ran against the coin's 20-day return.
findings.F4: The book carries almost no gain from the market's own rise (drift part -0.000017 a bar), so it trails holding in rising years: in 2020 the book earned 0.00024 a day against the coin's 0.00524, and in 2021 0.00045 against 0.00382. This is why its Sharpe is 0.15 below holding's.
findings.F5: The deepest falls are long and slow rather than single shocks.
findings.F6: The gain rises with the volatility ratio: in the top quartile of 20-day volatility over its 60-day mean, active bars earn 0.0060 long and 0.0024 short. The lower quartiles earn between -0.0012 and +0.0017.

ideas.idea: On a coin's high-volatility days, measured by its 20-day volatility, the next day's return runs against the day just closed, only while that day's move runs against the coin's 20-day return. The larger that day's return relative to its 20-day volatility, the larger the move back over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans for one day against a large counter-trend day in a volatile spell, such as a sharp drop inside a 20-day rise, and refuses to fade a large day that goes with the 20-day trend.
ideas.name: counter-trend volatile day reversal

ideas.idea: On a coin's high-volatility days, measured by its 20-day volatility, the next day's return runs against the day just closed. The larger that day's return relative to its 20-day volatility, and the higher the 20-day volatility stands above its 60-day average, the larger the move back over the next 1 day.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans hardest against large daily moves when volatility has just expanded well above its usual level, and lets the lean shrink toward nothing as volatility returns to normal, which saves fees on bets too small to pay.
ideas.name: volatility-expansion graded one-day reversal
